subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Cable Corrosion: The Silent Killer
description: A quick win: understand Cable Corrosion: The Silent Killer.

hook.text: The Williamsburg Bridge in New York lost 40% of its cable strength before anyone noticed.

buildup.text: Water seeps into cable wrapping, reaches the steel wires inside, and rusts them from within.

discovery.text: Engineers can't see inside cables without unwrapping them. Inspections require cutting open the protective cover.

twist.text: Acoustic monitoring now detects wire snaps inside cables. Each broken wire makes a distinct sound.

climax.text: Dehumidification systems pump dry air through cables to prevent moisture. Prevention beats repair.

punchline.text: The most dangerous damage is the kind you can't see.

quiz.question: How do engineers now detect broken wires inside suspension bridge cables?
options: X-ray machines scan the full length of every cable
Acoustic sensors detect the distinct sound each wire makes when it snaps
Drones fly alongside cables and photograph surface cracks
